info.title: Nightmail API
info.description: Send, receive and reply to email on your own domains. 202 means queued, not delivered.

x-quickstart.title: Add and verify your domain
x-quickstart.text: In the dashboard, open Domains and add it, or call POST /v1/domains with {"name":"acme.com"}. Publish the DNS records it returns at your DNS provider. Sending works once GET /v1/domains/{id} reports sending: "verified", usually within minutes of the records resolving. A domain whose records are still unproven after 72 hours is released.

x-quickstart.title: Create an API key
x-quickstart.text: In the dashboard, open API keys in the sidebar and choose Create key. A Send only key restricted to your domain is enough to send; it can’t read logs, so add Read permission if your code should look up outcomes. Store it as NIGHTMAIL_API_KEY on your server and never ship it to a browser.

x-quickstart.title: Send
x-quickstart.text: 202 means queued, not delivered. Follow the outcome in the dashboard’s Logs, or with GET /v1/emails/{id} and a key that has Read permission (a Send only key gets 403). Leave out region: the sender domain decides it. To test without reaching a real inbox, send to success@simulator.amazonses.com (or bounce@, complaint@, ooto@ and suppressionlist@ the same domain). Simulator sends use your daily sending limit like any other send, but never count towards your sender score.
x-quickstart.code:
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://nightmail.dev/v1/emails/send' \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $NIGHTMAIL_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  --data '{"from":"hello@acme.com","to":"you@acme.com","subject":"Hello from Nightmail","text":"It works."}'

x-quickstart.title: Receive (optional)
x-quickstart.text: Publish the receiving MX record from the domain page. Hosted Nightmail receives on a free subdomain such as reply.<your domain>, so the domain’s existing mailboxes keep working; it uses the domain itself only when its MX already points to Nightmail, or when you choose it. Create an address with POST /v1/inbound/addresses and subscribe to message.received with POST /v1/inbound/webhooks.

x-quickstart.title: Reply
x-quickstart.text: POST /v1/inbound/threads/{threadId}/reply answers the newest message from its receiving address and sets In-Reply-To and References.

bearerAuth.description: A Nightmail API key. Credentials never belong in URLs.

dashboardSession.name: nightmail.session_token
dashboardSession.description: OIDC-authenticated HttpOnly session for local development. Unsafe requests require the canonical dashboard Origin. A browser holds one session per connected account (nightmail.session_token, then nightmail.session_token.1 to .4); X-Nightmail-Account (the account ID from getCurrentIdentity) chooses the one a request acts as, otherwise the browser default. A named account without a live session gets 401 ACCOUNT_SIGNED_OUT, never another account.

secureDashboardSession.name: __Host-nightmail.session_token
secureDashboardSession.description: OIDC-authenticated Secure HttpOnly host-only session in production. Unsafe requests require the canonical dashboard Origin. A browser holds one session per connected account (__Host-nightmail.session_token, then __Host-nightmail.session_token.1 to .4); X-Nightmail-Account (the account ID from getCurrentIdentity) chooses the one a request acts as, otherwise the browser default. A named account without a live session gets 401 ACCOUNT_SIGNED_OUT, never another account.

id.description: Recipe ID from listRuleRecipes.

params.description: The recipe’s fields by name, normalized.

resetAt.description: Next capacity change for a Hosted rolling send limit.

details.description: Every problem found, when there is more than one part, such as rule diagnostics with rule, line, column, message and hint, or a measurement, such as CONTENT_TOO_LARGE_TO_SCREEN with screenedBytes and limitBytes (and index in a batch).

permission.description: The permission: sendEmail, sentMail, receivedMail, inboxes, audience (audience and content), receivingRules or configuration.

level.description: The level of that permission: on (sendEmail), read or write. With person alone, what the person's MCP sign-in must be approved for.

scope.description: What the credential's scope must cover: workspace (no sender-domain limit), allAddresses (every receiving address), domain:<name> or address:<address>.

credential.description: The kind of credential: dashboard (a signed-in dashboard session), signIn (an MCP sign-in), lasting (anything but a temporary agent token) or notDelegated (a dashboard session, or an API key no MCP approval made).

person.description: A person, never a key: a signed-in dashboard session or their own MCP sign-in, with this role in the workspace (admin is an owner or admin). The workspace, its members, invitations and billing are a person's.

required.description: On a 403 permission refusal: what the request needs that this credential lacks. The Nightmail-Required-Permission header says the same.

workspaceId.description: One of your workspaces. Until one is set, calls use your only workspace, else the one you used last.

receiving.description: Deprecated and ignored: receiving follows the role.

id.description: The sign-in (mcp_…).

profile.description: The label of the client entry that connected (?profile= on its MCP URL). Display only.

own.description: Your own sign-in. Otherwise another member's agent that made agent tokens in this workspace (owners and admins see these).

permissions.description: What the sign-in was approved for, before your role in each workspace narrows it.

workspaceId.description: Your sign-ins: the default workspace for calls that name none. Null otherwise.

lastUsedAt.description: The latest use of the sign-in or of one of its agent tokens here.

tokens.description: Short-lived agent tokens it made in this workspace, newest first (at most 20). Revoking the agent revokes them.

state.description: awaiting_role: waiting for the BYO stack. provisioning: verifying regional resources and importing verified domains. ready: sending allowed once the tenant is ready. failed: the last setup attempt failed; verify again.

tenant.description: Hosted only: the SES tenant that isolates this workspace. Sends are rejected with TENANT_NOT_READY until it is ready. BYO connections are always ready.

sendingPause.description: Hosted reputation hold: sending and dispatch are paused until operator review. Receiving is unaffected.

cap.description: Recipients allowed per rolling 24 hours. Null when this workspace has no daily limit: in good standing (GET /v1/sender-score) or exempt.

used.description: Recipients charged in the current rolling 24 hours, including SES simulator addresses.

resetAt.description: When capacity next frees up or the limit changes.

nextCap.description: After a resume, the limit that applies when its reduced limit ends; null otherwise, and null when no daily limit follows.

sendingLimit.description: Hosted only: the daily limit (set by the sender score) that POST /v1/emails/send enforces with 429 SEND_LIMIT_REACHED.

standing.description: Hosted only: the enforcement step summary. GET /v1/sender-score has the reasons, the limit math and what an owner can release.

domains.description: Domains of its own the workspace claimed and how many can send. The built-in domain is not one of them.

sent.description: Whether this workspace has any sent email in its log (test sends included; the log keeps 30 days).

received.description: Whether this workspace has received any email (kept as long as its received mail is).

id.description: Its ID in listDomains, once it is set up on this connection.

sending.description: ready: it sends now (in a new workspace's first seconds, a send waits for its setup to finish). pending: it is being set up. closed: a domain of the workspace's own verified, so it only receives now. off: it sends nothing: turned off by the operator, or paused with every built-in domain (paused).

paused.description: Present while sending from every built-in domain is paused (the circuit breaker on their shared reputation) until an operator turns it back on. Mail still queued from it when it paused was canceled; it keeps receiving.

scope.description: Who it sends to: anyone, or the verified addresses of the workspace's members.

used.description: Recipients it sent to in the rolling 24 hours, counted as perDay counts them; 0 once it no longer sends.

builtinDomain.description: Hosted only: the subdomain of the installation's own domain this workspace sends and receives on before it verifies a domain of its own (sendEmail from any address at it), with who it sends to and its recipient caps. Absent when the installation has none; null until this workspace has one.

attention.description: A connected AWS account's most pressing health finding, for a banner; absent when nothing needs attention.

ConnectionSummary.description: The current workspace's hosted sending connection; null when self-hosted.

type.description: workspace: the whole workspace, with permissions and domains. addresses: only mail at receiving addresses. inbox: only one agent inbox; the key stops working when the inbox is deleted.

addressIds.description: addresses: the receiving addresses it may use, or null for every address including ones added later. inbox: the inbox. Null for workspace keys.

inboxId.description: inbox: the agent inbox the key belongs to.

mail.description: addresses and inbox: read (mail, events, attachments), send (reply and start conversations from those addresses only), modify (mark read, archive, star, label, delete an inbox), create (create agent inboxes and use the ones it created). Empty for workspace keys.

createdInboxIds.description: With create: the live agent inboxes the key created, which it reaches as well as addressIds (up to 1,000, by ID). Empty otherwise.

active.description: Every approval that owns it is active, so a key is accepted and a webhook is delivered to. False: a key is refused and a webhook is not delivered to until all of them are active again.

endsAt.description: The earliest end among its owners: when it stops working unless their agents connect again before then.

owners.description: Each approval that owns it, by ID. A key has one; a webhook has one for each approval that set it up or changed it.

ApprovalTie.description: Set when this is tied to MCP approvals: created, or for a webhook set up or changed, over MCP with a person’s sign-in or with a key that is tied. It works only while every one of them is active. Null: it lasts, not tied to any approval.

id.description: An agent sign-in (mcp_…) that owns it, as listAgents lists it.

endsAt.description: When this approval ends: 30 days after its agent last connected, and no later than 90 days after the person approved the agent. Each connection moves it later, up to that limit; removing the approval ends it at once.

active.description: This approval is active: not revoked or ended, with the manage scope, and its person an owner or admin here.

action.description: What happened, as <area>.<verb>: api_key.create, member.role_change, domain.delete, support.view.

type.description: member is a signed-in person; support is Nightmail support reading with your permission; system is Nightmail itself.

label.description: A short display name for the actor, such as a key name, or null.

email.description: The member’s email address, for member actors.

ApiKeyLastChange.description: The newest entry in its history (listApiKeyChanges): when it was created, changed or revoked, and by whom. Null when none is kept (after a year).

permissions.description: Workspace permissions. Empty for a key limited to addresses or an inbox: see access.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working: the expiry set on it, or for an inbox key its inbox's end if that is sooner. Null: it never expires. updateApiKey changes it on the same secret.

client.description: What the agent said it is (client_name), its claim, never verified. Null when it didn't say.

agent.description: A key an agent got through agent setup (exchangeAgentSetupToken or the device flow): the agent it was made for. Null for every other key.

name.description: Any text, 1 to 100 characters once trimmed. Need not be unique.

domains.description: Workspace keys: sender domains it is limited to, including their subdomains. Defaults to all.

addressIds.description: Receiving address IDs. Omit for every address, including ones added later. [] with create: only the inboxes the key creates.

inboxId.description: An active agent inbox. The key stops working when the inbox is deleted, and when an expiring inbox ends.

CreateApiKeyAccess.description: What the key is limited to. Defaults to the workspace. A key for addresses or an inbox takes its permissions in access.mail and can never send from other addresses, read other mail or manage the workspace.

addDomains.description: Workspace keys: adds these sender domains and keeps the others. A key for all domains already has them.

removeDomains.description: Workspace keys: removes these sender domains. Removing the last one is refused, since [] means all domains: set domains instead.

expiresAt.description: Any key: sets when it stops working, or null so it never expires (an inbox key then ends with its inbox). An expired key can be given a later expiry: it works again with the same secret. Over MCP, an agent moves an expiry later only up to its own approval's end, and never removes one; a key an approval created is exempt, as it ends with that approval anyway.

type.description: A key for addresses or an inbox: makes it the other one, on the same secret. inbox takes inboxId; addresses keeps the inbox as its address unless addressIds says otherwise.

inboxId.description: An inbox key: the active agent inbox it belongs to now. It ends with that inbox, and its expiry is at most that inbox's end.

addressIds.description: A key for addresses: replaces its addresses. null for every address, including ones added later.

addAddressIds.description: A key for addresses: adds these and keeps the others. An address it already has is left as it is, so a retry changes nothing.

removeAddressIds.description: A key for addresses: removes these. Requests with the key lose them at once, and replies it queued from them are not sent. An inbox the key created stays reachable while it has create, so removing one is refused (409 CREATED_INBOX_REACHABLE) unless mail drops create too.

mail.description: A key for addresses or an inbox: replaces what it may do with that mail: read, send, modify, and create (agent inboxes, which it then reaches as well).

access.description: A key limited to addresses or an inbox: what it reaches. A workspace key stays a workspace key, and a key for addresses or an inbox stays one of those two.

key.description: The API key (nm_…), shown once. Save it as NIGHTMAIL_API_KEY in the project's environment, never in code or a commit.

workspaceName.description: The workspace's name: tell the person, so they can confirm the key is in theirs.

permissions.description: read, send and manage, on every sender domain: send email, manage domains, inboxes, receiving, webhooks and campaigns. It can't create API keys, agent tokens, inbox connection keys, inbox keys or mail-client (IMAP/SMTP) passwords; members, billing and deleting the workspace are a person's.

RiskBreakdown.description: Rows flagged as risky. At preview, what the addresses say; once committed, the imported contacts campaigns skip, addresses that bounced elsewhere included. null for imports from before list hygiene.

consent.description: Records that everyone in this import agreed to receive marketing email. It changes only contacts with no consent decision yet: prior opt-outs stay unsubscribed and suppressed addresses stay suppressed. Omit it to import without consent.

id.description: The list’s ID.

name.description: The list’s name.

url.description: Dashboard URL for opening this newsletter.

name.description: Creates a new list with this name that is a newsletter.

from.description: The From address of its issues. Its domain need not be verified yet: the sender is checked when an issue is tested or sent.

listId.description: Makes this existing list a newsletter; 409 NEWSLETTER_EXISTS if it already is one.

from.description: The From address of its issues. Its domain need not be verified yet: the sender is checked when an issue is tested or sent.

CreateNewsletterInput.description: Exactly one of name (a new list) or listId (an existing list).

daily.description: One number per UTC day for the 182 days ending on the day of countedAt, oldest first: how many of these readers joined the list that day.

since.description: The first of those days, YYYY-MM-DD.

countedAt.description: When the count was taken; it includes every change made before then.

NewsletterReaders.description: Readers are the list’s members who are not deleted, not suppressed and subscribed to marketing, as campaign audiences count them. A list of up to 10,000 members is counted exactly when read. A larger list is counted in the background, a few minutes per pass, and read from its last count, which is refreshed when read more than an hour after it was taken; readers is null until the first count of a large list.

name.description: Renames the list.

from.description: The From address of its issues. Its domain need not be verified yet: the sender is checked when an issue is tested or sent.

listId.description: The list, which stays, with its contacts and its campaigns. Delete it with deleteContactList.

NewsletterDeleted.description: The list is no longer a newsletter. The list, its contacts and its campaigns are unchanged.

html.description: Nightmail block HTML shared with the visual editor and renderer. Email-safe inline styles support color, typography, spacing, borders, radius and dimensions. May use {{placeholders}}, as campaigns do: a campaign created from the template copies them and fills them from each contact and its own defaults. Call getContentGuide before writing.

unsubscribePageUrl.description: Your own unsubscribe or preference page: HTTPS, no user name, password, whitespace or unsubscribe_token parameter, at most 1,000 characters. The footer's Unsubscribe link opens it with unsubscribe_token=<token> added; your page records the opt-out by POSTing that token to /unsubscribe/<token> on this API (idempotent). List-Unsubscribe keeps this API's one-click address, which records the opt-out itself and, opened in a browser, confirms it and then continues to your page. Omit to use the hosted page.

url.description: Serves the 200 response (the base64 PNG as JSON) without a credential until expiresAt.

content.description: Base64 (standard or URL-safe alphabet; line breaks are accepted). No data URLs. At most 8 MiB decoded in JSON; upload larger files, up to 25 MiB, as raw bytes to POST /v1/attachments/upload.

domainId.description: The From domain’s ID (getDomain) when it is one of this workspace’s domains: where a finding with fixIn domain is fixed.

fix.description: What to do, in one short sentence of everyday words. The title and the detail name the header, record or standard.

fixIn.description: Where the fix is made: the From domain’s DNS records and setup (domain), the workspace’s settings (workspace), how much and to whom you send (sending), or the message itself (message).

headers.description: Header name to value. May include observed or planned transport headers; not trusted as authentication evidence.

attachments.description: Optional metadata only: decoded byte size, never attachment bytes or fetch URLs.

warnings.description: Recipients whose address looks risky (a disposable inbox, a mistyped provider, a role address): the email was queued anyway. Campaigns and marketing sends skip risky contacts.

scheduledAt.description: A scheduled send: when it goes (UTC).

SingleEmailQueued.description: For tracked sends, id is the transactional receipt, inboundMessageId identifies the stored message, and threadId identifies its conversation.

EmailScreenSummary.description: Content-screen outcome recorded at accept time when screening applies.

from.description: An address at a domain verified in this workspace, or at a subdomain of one. Hosted: also any address at the workspace’s built-in domain (connection.builtinDomain in GET /v1/me) until a domain of its own verifies.

region.description: Usually omitted: hosted Nightmail sends from the region bound to the sender domain, and a different value fails with SENDER_REGION_MISMATCH. Self-hosted installations default to their default region.

kind.description: marketing adds Nightmail's footer (an Unsubscribe link, with the workspace's postal address under it when it has one) and the one-click List-Unsubscribe headers.

data.description: JSON substitution data, including nested objects and arrays, is passed unchanged to SES. SES stored templates do not automatically escape HTML: callers must escape untrusted values for their HTML context. Maximum serialized JSON length: 262,144 characters.

template.description: Uses native SES stored-template rendering and snapshots its rendered MIME. SES does not automatically escape HTML; callers must escape untrusted HTML-context values. Simulated deployments do not render AWS templates.

attachments.description: IDs of files uploaded first (uploadAttachment). One file is at most 8 MiB decoded when sent as base64 in JSON (POST /v1/attachments), or 25 MiB as raw bytes (POST /v1/attachments/upload, with the name URI-encoded in X-Nightmail-Filename and the type in Content-Type). One email carries at most 100 files and 25 MiB of them together, decoded. A workspace keeps at most 100 GiB of uploaded files. For anything larger, link to the file from the email.

headers.description: Extra MIME headers, 8 KB total. The 15-header limit includes generated headers (two for marketing and any mailbox threading headers). Any name is allowed except headers Nightmail controls: From, Sender, Reply-To, Return-Path, To, Cc, Bcc, Subject, Date, Message-ID, MIME-Version, Content-*, DKIM-*, ARC-*, Authentication-Results, Received*, Resent-*, X-SES-*, List-Unsubscribe*, Auto-Submitted, and reply, receipt, trace and transport headers (Mail-Reply-To, Mail-Followup-To, Followup-To, Disposition-Notification-*, Return-Receipt-To, Errors-To, Bounces-To, Delivered-To, X-Original-To, DomainKey-*, Feedback-ID, TLS-Required, BIMI-*, Autocrypt*, OpenPGP). In-Reply-To and References must be <id@domain> Message-IDs and thread the message in the recipient's mail client.

topicId.description: kind marketing only (422 TOPIC_REQUIRES_MARKETING otherwise): the topic it is about (listTopics). A recipient who opted out of the topic is refused (reason topic_unsubscribed), and its one-click unsubscribe opts out of this topic only.

screen.description: Request outbound harm screening at accept time for live transactional mail. Hosted live screening is operator-controlled and cannot be disabled by setting this field to false. Simulated mail is not screened. A positive reject verdict fails the request synchronously with 422 CONTENT_REJECTED_SPAM (nothing queued); during a temporary outage of both classifiers, the message is accepted (202) and held unscreened until a classifier answers. Mandatory Hosted screening with no classifier configured returns retryable 503 CONTENT_SCREEN_UNAVAILABLE with Retry-After.

replyAddressId.description: Track a conversation through this receivable address. Use explicit subject and text/html. Requires unrestricted manage permission; From and Reply-To must belong to the address.

scheduledAt.description: Send at this time instead of now: an RFC 3339 instant with Z or an offset, such as 2026-11-20T09:00:00Z; times without an offset are refused, and the time is returned in UTC. From now (up to a minute in the past, which sends at once) to 30 days ahead; up to 100,000 scheduled emails may wait per workspace (SCHEDULED_EMAIL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED). Content screening and suppression are checked at accept time; sending limits and the balance apply at scheduledAt, when an email they refuse is rejected with their code (email.rejected), except Hosted marketing its ramp hour has no room for, which is held until there is (RAMP_LIMIT_REACHED in sendEmail's description). Not with replyAddressId.

warnings.description: Recipients whose address looks risky (a disposable inbox, a mistyped provider, a role address): the email was queued anyway. Campaigns and marketing sends skip risky contacts.

emails.description: Up to 100 messages. Their html and text together may hold 10 MiB (413 BATCH_CONTENT_TOO_LARGE).

from.description: An address at a domain verified in this workspace, or at a subdomain of one. Hosted: also any address at the workspace’s built-in domain (connection.builtinDomain in GET /v1/me) until a domain of its own verifies.

region.description: Usually omitted: hosted Nightmail sends from the region bound to the sender domain, and a different value fails with SENDER_REGION_MISMATCH. Self-hosted installations default to their default region.

kind.description: marketing adds Nightmail's footer (an Unsubscribe link, with the workspace's postal address under it when it has one) and the one-click List-Unsubscribe headers.

data.description: JSON substitution data, including nested objects and arrays, is passed unchanged to SES. SES stored templates do not automatically escape HTML: callers must escape untrusted values for their HTML context. Maximum serialized JSON length: 262,144 characters.

template.description: Uses native SES stored-template rendering and snapshots its rendered MIME. SES does not automatically escape HTML; callers must escape untrusted HTML-context values. Simulated deployments do not render AWS templates.

attachments.description: IDs of files uploaded first (uploadAttachment). One file is at most 8 MiB decoded when sent as base64 in JSON (POST /v1/attachments), or 25 MiB as raw bytes (POST /v1/attachments/upload, with the name URI-encoded in X-Nightmail-Filename and the type in Content-Type). One email carries at most 100 files and 25 MiB of them together, decoded. A workspace keeps at most 100 GiB of uploaded files. For anything larger, link to the file from the email.

headers.description: Extra MIME headers, 8 KB total. The 15-header limit includes generated headers (two for marketing and any mailbox threading headers). Any name is allowed except headers Nightmail controls: From, Sender, Reply-To, Return-Path, To, Cc, Bcc, Subject, Date, Message-ID, MIME-Version, Content-*, DKIM-*, ARC-*, Authentication-Results, Received*, Resent-*, X-SES-*, List-Unsubscribe*, Auto-Submitted, and reply, receipt, trace and transport headers (Mail-Reply-To, Mail-Followup-To, Followup-To, Disposition-Notification-*, Return-Receipt-To, Errors-To, Bounces-To, Delivered-To, X-Original-To, DomainKey-*, Feedback-ID, TLS-Required, BIMI-*, Autocrypt*, OpenPGP). In-Reply-To and References must be <id@domain> Message-IDs and thread the message in the recipient's mail client.

topicId.description: kind marketing only (422 TOPIC_REQUIRES_MARKETING otherwise): the topic it is about (listTopics). A recipient who opted out of the topic is refused (reason topic_unsubscribed), and its one-click unsubscribe opts out of this topic only.

screen.description: Request outbound harm screening at accept time for live transactional mail. Hosted live screening is operator-controlled and cannot be disabled by setting this field to false. Simulated mail is not screened. A positive reject verdict fails the request synchronously with 422 CONTENT_REJECTED_SPAM (nothing queued); during a temporary outage of both classifiers, the message is accepted (202) and held unscreened until a classifier answers. Mandatory Hosted screening with no classifier configured returns retryable 503 CONTENT_SCREEN_UNAVAILABLE with Retry-After.

html.description: Untrusted offline document; render only as the srcdoc of an iframe with sandbox="". Empty for classic Outlook (lint only).
HTML to preview, up to 256 KiB in UTF-8.

device.description: Viewport width in CSS pixels: mobile 390, desktop 800. Defaults to mobile for iOS, Android and Samsung Email; otherwise desktop.

emailId.description: Outbound email with retained HTML visible to this credential.

device.description: Viewport width in CSS pixels: mobile 390, desktop 800. Defaults to mobile for iOS, Android and Samsung Email; otherwise desktop.

EmailPreviewInput.description: Supply exactly one source: html or emailId.

untrustedContent.description: True for replies and older non-campaign mail of unknown origin: the subject or body may contain received content.

status.description: A scheduled email is queued, with scheduled true, until it is sent at scheduledAt.

suppressionReason.description: Reason recorded when this send was suppressed. For a multi-recipient send blocked locally, this is the first blocked recipient in To, Cc, Bcc order.

scheduled.description: True while a scheduled send waits for scheduledAt: it has not started sending, and cancelEmail or rescheduleEmail still apply. At that time it is admitted like a send made then (limits and balance included) and follows the usual lifecycle, or is rejected with the refusal’s code.

scheduledAt.description: When a scheduled send goes (UTC). Also set while queued mail waits to be retried.

createdAt.description: When the email was submitted; a scheduled send’s moves to the moment it was released at its time.

suppressedAt.description: When the address was suppressed (UTC). Null when it is not suppressed, and for a suppression from before these dates were kept.

suppressionReason.description: Reason recorded when this send was suppressed. For a multi-recipient send blocked locally, this is the first blocked recipient in To, Cc, Bcc order.

diagnosticCode.description: A bounce or a delay: the receiving server’s reply as SES reported it, such as "smtp; 550 5.1.1 user unknown". Written by the receiving server: untrusted text, to read as data, that can hold the recipient’s address, host names and IP addresses. On the email’s own events (getEmailDetail, listEmailEvents) it is up to 500 characters, as one line without control or invisible characters. In a webhook payload and the webhook delivery log, the addresses and IP addresses in it are replaced by pattern (<address>, <ip>) and it is up to 160 characters. For several recipients, the first that has one. Absent when SES reported none, for a bounce SES generated itself (its suppression list, its address validation), and on events stored before this field.

delayType.description: A delay: SES’s reason, such as MailboxFull, SpamDetected, RecipientServerError, TransientCommunicationFailure, IPFailure or General.

expirationTime.description: A delay: when SES stops retrying the delivery (UTC).

data.description: What the event recorded. An email the content screen refused says so in code (CONTENT_REJECTED_SPAM) and nothing more: the screen’s score, its model and its threshold are never part of an event or a webhook payload.

id.description: The conversation (getInboundThread).

count.description: Messages in it that the caller can read.

messages.description: Up to 50 of them around this email, oldest first.

EmailThread.description: The conversation: of a reply from a receiving address or inbox, or of an email whose In-Reply-To named a stored message its sender could read, with the messages around it that you can read. Null for an email in none, when you can read none of the conversation's received or stored messages, and for credentials that cannot read received mail.

id.description: The stored message (getInboundMessage). An email sent with sendEmail that joined the conversation by answering one of its messages has no stored copy: its email ID.

emailId.description: The sent email (getEmailDetail) of an outbound message; null for received mail.

at.description: When it was received or sent.

status.description: Received mail: received. Sent mail: the email status (scheduled while it waits for its time).

untrustedContent.description: True for replies and older non-campaign mail of unknown origin: the subject or body may contain received content.

scheduledAt.description: The new send time: an RFC 3339 instant with Z or an offset, returned in UTC.

content.description: Base64 (standard or URL-safe alphabet; line breaks are accepted). No data URLs. At most 8 MiB decoded in JSON; upload larger files, up to 25 MiB, as raw bytes to POST /v1/attachments/upload.

url.description: Dashboard URL for opening this campaign. Drafts open in the editor; launched campaigns open in review.

counts.description: Counts of immutable campaign email records grouped by their current status, not cumulative provider events or delivery rates. Drafts with no queued emails have zero counts.

priority.description: Send order: contacts whose property equals an earlier value are reviewed and released first; everyone else follows. Useful with paced sending, e.g. { property: "plan", values: ["active", "former"] }.

unsubscribePageUrl.description: Your own unsubscribe or preference page: HTTPS, no user name, password, whitespace or unsubscribe_token parameter, at most 1,000 characters. The footer's Unsubscribe link opens it with unsubscribe_token=<token> added; your page records the opt-out by POSTing that token to /unsubscribe/<token> on this API (idempotent). List-Unsubscribe keeps this API's one-click address, which records the opt-out itself and, opened in a browser, confirms it and then continues to your page. Omit to use the hosted page.

topicId.description: The topic the campaign is about (listTopics): it skips contacts who opted out of it, and its one-click unsubscribe opts out of this topic only. Not on a required notice.

requiredNotice.description: A required notice: a message every recipient must get whatever their marketing choice, such as a change to terms, prices or taxes, never a promotion. It goes to everyone in the audience who is not suppressed, people who unsubscribed from marketing included, without an Unsubscribe link or List-Unsubscribe header, and is paced, limited and paused like any campaign. Only where an operator turned required notices on for the workspace (requiredNotices in getWorkspaceSettings); 403 REQUIRED_NOTICES_OFF otherwise. Sending or scheduling one needs confirmRequiredNotice. Turned off later, a launched notice pauses before releasing anyone more (pause reason REQUIRED_NOTICES_OFF) and is resumed or rescheduled only once they are on again. Resumed after a list-probe quarantine, it goes on to everyone captured for it (never deliveredOnly).

CampaignDraft.description: Drafts may omit sender, subject, content and audience until review or send, except that domain-restricted keys must supply a From address on one of their domains. Content is block HTML (see html); the same form is what the dashboard composer reads and writes, so people and agents edit one document. Simple {{name}} personalization works in text and quoted href/alt attributes; values are HTML-escaped and rendered URLs are validated. Durable campaign preparation is bounded and runs in background jobs.

total.description: Fixed recipient count once the audience is frozen (recipients expected while a large audience is being captured).

expanded.description: Recipients materialized as immutable email records.

canceled.description: Recipients canceled before materialization. Materialized cancellations remain in counts.byStatus.canceled.

error.description: Why the campaign failed or was canceled by the system.

perDay.description: Maximum recipients released per rolling 24-hour window; null means no daily cap.

autoPause.description: Pause automatically when bounce or complaint rates exceed safe thresholds.

rateShare.description: Maximum fraction of the SES per-second send rate this campaign uses; 1 is the full rate.

windowExpanded.description: Recipients released in the current 24-hour window.

nextWindowAt.description: When the next 24-hour window opens, when a daily cap is set.

plan.description: Sent with the recommended plan: its daily batches (one 24-hour window each; the last repeats). Null otherwise.

batch.description: With a plan: the batch the current window releases, from 1.

size.description: Recipients the first day starts with.

waitMinutes.description: Minutes it then waits for their bounces and rejections before the rest of the day's batch.

firstBatch.description: With a plan: its first day's small batch and the wait after it.

consent.description: The consent source confirmed at launch, if any.

deliveredOnly.description: After a resumed list-probe quarantine: the rest goes only to contacts this workspace delivered to before; the others are counted in canceled. Never for a required notice.

linkHold.description: When present, the daily pacing window is the shared link allowance, or the link record is held for operator review.

waiting.description: Why releasing recipients is currently held, and the best estimate of until when. list_probe: Hosted sent the first recipients (the list probe) and waits for their bounces and complaints before releasing the rest. feedback_lag: releasing is briefly held while priority safety feedback (bounces/complaints) catches up. ramp: a Hosted sender's first large campaigns release in growing hourly steps (sendEstimate.ramp); this hour's step is used up, or its delivery results are still coming in before the next step. link_record: the campaign has no host for its unsubscribe link right now (its workspace's sending is paused, or with own link hosts, its domain's isn't active yet); it continues by itself.

feedbackLag.description: Present while a campaign is preparing, sending, or paused when delivery feedback ingestion is at least 2 minutes behind.

CampaignDelivery.description: The current launch: null until the campaign is sent or scheduled, and cleared by a new revision.

recipients.description: Recipients still to release: for a draft, the last audience count (previewCampaignAudience; null before one); once launched, those not released yet.

ratePerSecond.description: The region's send rate the campaign plans at, per second, before its rate share; null until the region's quota was read.

seconds.description: How long releasing the recipients left takes from when it starts (the campaign's last change, updatedAt, or scheduledAt): from the ramp, the daily cap (pacing.perDay), the rate share and the region's send rate. A draft is estimated without a daily cap at the full rate. An estimate: it assumes clean, prompt feedback and leaves out the list probe's wait, quota holds and other mail sharing the rate. Null when it cannot be told (no audience count or send rate yet).

finishAt.description: A launched campaign: when its last recipient is expected to be released, as of its last change (updatedAt or scheduledAt, plus seconds). Null for a draft, while paused or failed, or when it cannot be told.

CampaignSendEstimate.description: How long sending takes, for a draft or a campaign that has recipients left to release. Null for a finished or canceled campaign; lists leave it out.

step.description: The step the campaign releases at, from 1.

steps.description: How many steps the ramp has; past the last one only the other limits apply.

ceilingPerHour.description: Most recipients this step releases in its hour.

startedAt.description: When this step's hour started: its first release. Null before it.

released.description: Recipients released since this step's hour started.

CampaignRamp.description: Where the campaign is on the ramp. A Hosted sender's first large campaigns release in hourly steps that grow (1,000 an hour at first), moving to the next step once an hour at this one went out and its delivery results are in and clean; more than 3% bounces or more than 0.08% complaints (at least 2) in a step pause the campaign. The first step not already proven by the workspace's largest clean marketing hour of the last 30 days is where it starts, so an established sender skips it. Null when no ramp applies (self-hosted, your own AWS account, simulated mail, an established sender, or past the last step). Transactional mail never waits for it.

html.description: Block HTML: h1-h3, p, ul/ol, blockquote, pre>code, hr, img, buttons, columns and styled sections with inline formatting. A constrained email-safe style attribute supports color, typography, spacing, borders, radius and dimensions; arbitrary CSS remains rejected. No wrappers, tables, class or id. Call getContentGuide in MCP or GET /v1/campaign-content-guide for the full vocabulary and examples.

templateId.description: Copies the active published revision of this global campaign template into a new independent campaign draft.

url.description: Dashboard URL for opening this campaign. Drafts open in the editor; launched campaigns open in review.

Listing never counts emails or events; listing with listId starts a count for finished campaigns whose figures are missing or stale, so they appear on a later read.

totals.description: Lifetime distinct email counts from current state and stored events; outcomes overlap. Accepted excludes simulated mail; other outcomes include simulated events for simulated mail. Opens and clicks include bots and privacy proxies. Failed means rejected or rendering failed; suppressed, canceled and uncertain mail remain in counts.byStatus.

value.description: Fraction, not percent. Both counts exclude simulated emails. Null when the denominator is zero or engagement tracking is disabled. Not clamped: delayed feedback can temporarily make outcomes exceed the denominator.

delivery.description: Delivered / accepted. Receiving-server acceptance, not inbox placement.

value.description: Fraction, not percent. Both counts exclude simulated emails. Null when the denominator is zero or engagement tracking is disabled. Not clamped: delayed feedback can temporarily make outcomes exceed the denominator.

click.description: Unique clicked emails / delivered, not click-to-open rate.

computedAt.description: When counts, totals and rates were counted: they include every change made before then. state and delivery are always current.

CampaignStats.description: Lifetime campaign statistics, with no date cutoff or pagination. Done means dispatch finished, not delivery finished. Feedback is asynchronous; missing engagement does not prove nobody read or clicked. Simulated outcomes are never evidence of real delivery.

html.description: Complete rendered email document; empty when the draft has no content.

risky.description: Contacts who could receive it but are flagged as risky (a disposable inbox, a mistyped provider, a role address, an address known to be undeliverable): the send skips them. Not in eligible.

verdict.description: ready: send as you like. ramp_recommended: the plan is suggested. ramp_required: a Hosted send this large, from a new domain or far above anything its domain has sent, goes out with the plan (pacing.plan "recommended"), a daily limit no larger than its first day, or a confirmed consent source (consent); 422 RAMP_REQUIRED otherwise.

summary.description: Why, in one or two plain sentences, when a ramp is recommended or required.

reasons.description: The findings behind the verdict in the original codes, one per code: a newly registered domain, one new here and a new link domain read NEW_DOMAIN, a jump over the usual day SIZE_JUMP; blocklist findings appear only in findings. Prefer findings.

findings.description: Every finding behind the verdict, with its own code: NEW_REGISTRATION (registered recently, from public registry data), NEW_HERE (registered long ago, new to this workspace), NEW_DOMAIN (added recently, registration not known), USUAL_JUMP, NEW_LINK_DOMAIN, BLOCKLISTED_BEFORE (an earlier send drew replies naming a blocklist and none has finished without since), BLOCKLIST_UNCOUNTED (a recent send's blocklist replies aren't counted yet, so it isn't taken for clean), and the original codes.

firstSeenAt.description: When the From domain (or the domain it is under) was added to this workspace.

ageDays.description: Days since it was added to this workspace: its history here, not its age.

registeredAt.description: When its registrable domain was registered (YYYY-MM-DD), from public registry data; null when not known (never taken for old).

registeredDays.description: Days since registeredAt; null when not known.

name.description: The registrable domain the links go on, when it is not the From domain's.

dmarc.description: The DMARC policy last observed; null when not checked yet.

mailFrom.description: The custom MAIL FROM domain (aligned SPF).

sharedLinkPacing.description: This campaign shares the link domain’s daily sending allowance.

linkHost.description: Kept for compatibility, always not_configured: ownLinkHost and linkOrigin say where the links go.

active.description: true: the links go there. false: it isn’t set up yet, so they go on linkOrigin (the link domain) meanwhile.

ownLinkHost.description: The domain's own link host, when this workspace has them; null without one.

linkOrigin.description: Where this campaign's links (its unsubscribe link, the text part's, List-Unsubscribe and linked images) go if it launches now: the domain's own link host when active, else the link domain (Hosted) or this installation's own origin. Null when the launch would be refused for want of one (the workspace's sending is paused, or no link host for the domain). A launch on the link domain moves to the domain's own host for the copies made once that is active.

largestSend.description: Most recipients SES accepted from one campaign in the last 90 days.

firstSentAt.description: When this workspace first had mail accepted (workspace history only); null with none.

usualDay.description: The usual day: the median of the mail accepted on the days it sent in the last 14 days (workspace history only); 0 with none.

sent.description: Recipients SES accepted in the last 30 days.

bounceRate.description: Hard bounces ÷ accepted over the last 30 days; null with nothing sent.

complaintRate.description: Complaints ÷ accepted over the last 30 days; null with nothing sent.

workspace.description: Every kind of mail the workspace sent; largestSend counts campaigns.

neverMailed.description: Recipients who joined the list since it was last sent to (or ever, when it never was) and have no open or click on record; null when counting took too long.

usualJump.description: This send ÷ the workspace's usual day (history.workspace.usualDay); null without one.

plan.description: The recommended daily batches; null when one day covers everyone.

by.description: Kept as it was: a newly registered domain reads NEW_DOMAIN and a blocklist SIZE_JUMP. reason says which.

readiness.description: With readiness=true: the send review of a marketing campaign with a sender; null for a required notice or a draft without a sender.

defaults.description: Up to 100 key/value pairs, at most 64 KiB of JSON total.

unsubscribePageUrl.description: Your own unsubscribe or preference page: HTTPS, no user name, password, whitespace or unsubscribe_token parameter, at most 1,000 characters. The footer's Unsubscribe link opens it with unsubscribe_token=<token> added; your page records the opt-out by POSTing that token to /unsubscribe/<token> on this API (idempotent). List-Unsubscribe keeps this API's one-click address, which records the opt-out itself and, opened in a browser, confirms it and then continues to your page. Omit to use the hosted page.

topicId.description: The topic the campaign is about (listTopics): it skips contacts who opted out of it, and its one-click unsubscribe opts out of this topic only. Not on a required notice.

requiredNotice.description: A required notice: a message every recipient must get whatever their marketing choice, such as a change to terms, prices or taxes, never a promotion. It goes to everyone in the audience who is not suppressed, people who unsubscribed from marketing included, without an Unsubscribe link or List-Unsubscribe header, and is paced, limited and paused like any campaign. Only where an operator turned required notices on for the workspace (requiredNotices in getWorkspaceSettings); 403 REQUIRED_NOTICES_OFF otherwise. Sending or scheduling one needs confirmRequiredNotice. Turned off later, a launched notice pauses before releasing anyone more (pause reason REQUIRED_NOTICES_OFF) and is resumed or rescheduled only once they are on again. Resumed after a list-probe quarantine, it goes on to everyone captured for it (never deliveredOnly).

html.description: Block HTML: h1-h3, p, ul/ol, blockquote, pre>code, hr, img, buttons, columns and styled sections with inline formatting. A constrained email-safe style attribute supports color, typography, spacing, borders, radius and dimensions; arbitrary CSS remains rejected. No wrappers, tables, class or id. Call getContentGuide in MCP or GET /v1/campaign-content-guide for the full vocabulary and examples.

data.description: Up to 100 key/value pairs, at most 64 KiB of JSON total.

queued.description: Recipients expected (exact for lists up to 5,000 members and unsegmented lists once list counts are enabled; may be 0 if an uncounted large list exceeds the 200 ms launch budget without a prior preview); delivery.total is authoritative once the audience is frozen.

risky.description: Recipients the send skips as risky contacts, by reason: exact when queued is; null when a large audience could not be counted at launch.

verdict.description: ready: send as you like. ramp_recommended: the plan is suggested. ramp_required: a Hosted send this large, from a new domain or far above anything its domain has sent, goes out with the plan (pacing.plan "recommended"), a daily limit no larger than its first day, or a confirmed consent source (consent); 422 RAMP_REQUIRED otherwise.

summary.description: Why, in one or two plain sentences, when a ramp is recommended or required.

reasons.description: The findings behind the verdict in the original codes, one per code: a newly registered domain, one new here and a new link domain read NEW_DOMAIN, a jump over the usual day SIZE_JUMP; blocklist findings appear only in findings. Prefer findings.

findings.description: Every finding behind the verdict, with its own code: NEW_REGISTRATION (registered recently, from public registry data), NEW_HERE (registered long ago, new to this workspace), NEW_DOMAIN (added recently, registration not known), USUAL_JUMP, NEW_LINK_DOMAIN, BLOCKLISTED_BEFORE (an earlier send drew replies naming a blocklist and none has finished without since), BLOCKLIST_UNCOUNTED (a recent send's blocklist replies aren't counted yet, so it isn't taken for clean), and the original codes.

firstSeenAt.description: When the From domain (or the domain it is under) was added to this workspace.

ageDays.description: Days since it was added to this workspace: its history here, not its age.

registeredAt.description: When its registrable domain was registered (YYYY-MM-DD), from public registry data; null when not known (never taken for old).

registeredDays.description: Days since registeredAt; null when not known.

name.description: The registrable domain the links go on, when it is not the From domain's.

dmarc.description: The DMARC policy last observed; null when not checked yet.

mailFrom.description: The custom MAIL FROM domain (aligned SPF).

sharedLinkPacing.description: This campaign shares the link domain’s daily sending allowance.

linkHost.description: Kept for compatibility, always not_configured: ownLinkHost and linkOrigin say where the links go.

active.description: true: the links go there. false: it isn’t set up yet, so they go on linkOrigin (the link domain) meanwhile.

ownLinkHost.description: The domain's own link host, when this workspace has them; null without one.

linkOrigin.description: Where this campaign's links (its unsubscribe link, the text part's, List-Unsubscribe and linked images) go if it launches now: the domain's own link host when active, else the link domain (Hosted) or this installation's own origin. Null when the launch would be refused for want of one (the workspace's sending is paused, or no link host for the domain). A launch on the link domain moves to the domain's own host for the copies made once that is active.

largestSend.description: Most recipients SES accepted from one campaign in the last 90 days.

firstSentAt.description: When this workspace first had mail accepted (workspace history only); null with none.

usualDay.description: The usual day: the median of the mail accepted on the days it sent in the last 14 days (workspace history only); 0 with none.

sent.description: Recipients SES accepted in the last 30 days.

bounceRate.description: Hard bounces ÷ accepted over the last 30 days; null with nothing sent.

complaintRate.description: Complaints ÷ accepted over the last 30 days; null with nothing sent.

workspace.description: Every kind of mail the workspace sent; largestSend counts campaigns.

largestSend.description: Most recipients SES accepted from one campaign in the last 90 days.

firstSentAt.description: When this workspace first had mail accepted (workspace history only); null with none.

usualDay.description: The usual day: the median of the mail accepted on the days it sent in the last 14 days (workspace history only); 0 with none.

sent.description: Recipients SES accepted in the last 30 days.

bounceRate.description: Hard bounces ÷ accepted over the last 30 days; null with nothing sent.

complaintRate.description: Complaints ÷ accepted over the last 30 days; null with nothing sent.

neverMailed.description: Recipients who joined the list since it was last sent to (or ever, when it never was) and have no open or click on record; null when counting took too long.

lastSentAt.description: When a campaign last went to this list.

consent.description: The consent evidence it was imported with, if any.

sizeJump.description: This send ÷ the largest campaign its domain sent in the last 90 days; null without one.

usualJump.description: This send ÷ the workspace's usual day (history.workspace.usualDay); null without one.

batches.description: Recipients per day, in order: one batch a day, the most engaged first and never-mailed last.

size.description: Recipients the first day starts with.

waitMinutes.description: Minutes it then waits for their bounces and rejections before the rest of the day's batch.

firstBatch.description: The first day's small batch and wait, inside its batch; null when the first day is small already.

seconds.description: How long the plan takes from its start, the hourly ramp included.

plan.description: The recommended daily batches; null when one day covers everyone.

by.description: Kept as it was: a newly registered domain reads NEW_DOMAIN and a blocklist SIZE_JUMP. reason says which.

reason.description: What requires the ramp. BLOCKLISTED: mail from this From domain or with these links drew replies naming a blocklist and no send has finished without any since; a consent confirmation does not waive it.

maxPerDay.description: The largest daily limit that counts as a ramp: the plan's first day.

readiness.description: The send review as of the launch (list.neverMailed is not counted then); null for a required notice.

confirmRequiredNotice.description: Required for a required notice (422 REQUIRED_NOTICE_UNCONFIRMED without it): the sender confirms it is a required notice with no promotion. Recorded with who and when. An agent asks the person first.

perDay.description: Release at most this many recipients per rolling 24-hour window. Omit or null for no daily cap. Delivery always also respects the SES 24-hour quota.

autoPause.description: Pause automatically if the bounce rate exceeds 2% (after 1,000 accepted) or the complaint rate exceeds 0.08% (after 5,000 accepted). Hosted shared sending requires true; false is rejected.

rateShare.description: Maximum fraction of the SES per-second send rate this campaign may use; the rest stays free for transactional mail and other campaigns. Defaults to 0.5 for paced campaigns; campaigns sent without pacing use the full rate.

plan.description: Send in the daily batches previewCampaignAudience recommends (readiness.plan), worked out again at launch: the most engaged contacts first, never-mailed last. Not with perDay.

source.description: Where this list's consent comes from, for example "Signed up at checkout on our site since 2023".

CampaignConsentConfirmation.description: The sender confirms everyone on the list agreed to this mail, and where that consent comes from. Lets a send the review requires a ramp for (readiness.verdict ramp_required) go out without the plan. Stored with the campaign, with who and when, and in the workspace's Activity. An agent asks the person first.

confirmRequiredNotice.description: Required for a required notice (422 REQUIRED_NOTICE_UNCONFIRMED without it): the sender confirms it is a required notice with no promotion. Recorded with who and when. An agent asks the person first.

perDay.description: Release at most this many recipients per rolling 24-hour window. Omit to keep the current cap; null removes it. Delivery always also respects the SES 24-hour quota.

autoPause.description: Omit to keep the current setting. Hosted shared sending always enforces automatic pause; false is rejected.

rateShare.description: Omit to keep the current setting.

postalAddress.description: The postal address every campaign footer and marketing send shows under Unsubscribe; null until one is set. Campaigns can't be sent or scheduled without it.

requiredNotices.description: Whether campaigns in this workspace may be required notices (requiredNotice), which also reach people who unsubscribed from marketing. Only an operator turns this on.

focus.description: What the workspace is here for, the first leading: marketing emails, a newsletter, developer (transactional) emails, agent inboxes or a personal inbox. The dashboard tailors its first steps and Overview to it. Null until chosen; empty when skipped.

postalAddress.description: The workspace's postal address, as plain text: at most 300 characters on up to 6 lines, without HTML. Every campaign email and marketing send shows it under the Unsubscribe link, as US law (CAN-SPAM) requires; a campaign can't be sent or scheduled without it.

focus.description: What the workspace is here for, the first leading: marketing emails, a newsletter, developer (transactional) emails, agent inboxes or a personal inbox. The dashboard tailors its first steps and Overview to it. Null until chosen; empty when skipped. Order matters: the first leads.

used.description: Domains in the workspace, across every region and page.

limit.description: How many domains the workspace may have: 100 unless Nightmail set another limit on request.

quota.description: Hosted only, and only for credentials without domain restrictions. Absent when the workspace sends through its own AWS account, which has no domain total. Adding a domain past the limit fails with DOMAIN_LIMIT_REACHED; at most 10 of them may be unproven at once.

source.description: Domain publishing the effective TXT record; may be the organizational domain.

dmarc.description: Last DNS and SES observation for this From domain. Null when unchecked, unavailable or stale. Alignment describes configured identifiers, not a delivery verdict.

purpose.description: links: optional, the domain's own link host (links.<domain>) for the unsubscribe and other links Nightmail adds to campaign and marketing mail; shown when the installation has a link domain with Cloudflare for SaaS.

owner.description: The registrar or host, e.g. Porkbun.

target.description: What its record points to, e.g. pixie.porkbun.com.

parking.description: With wildcard: the answer is a registrar’s parking or forwarding record.

wildcard.description: With missing on a CNAME: a wildcard record (e.g. *.example.com) answers this name with an address instead, as it does a random name beside it. Add the CNAME exactly: the specific record wins over the wildcard.

state.description: found: public DNS has this record as listed (it may still take SES a few minutes to verify). missing: nothing of this type at the name. wrong_value: the name has a record of this type with another value.

values.description: wrong_value only: what public DNS has at the name instead (at most 5). Empty otherwise.

publicDns.description: For pending sending and MAIL FROM records: what public DNS (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1) shows for this record. verifyDomain looks it up now (answers cached up to 30 seconds). Other reads show the last background check, which runs every 15 to 60 minutes for a Hosted domain still pending an hour after it was added. Null when DNS did not answer in time; absent before any check and on other records.

name.description: The provider, e.g. Cloudflare, Vercel, Route 53, GoDaddy or Namecheap.

zone.description: The zone it hosts, which record names are relative to there.

url.description: The provider's DNS page for the zone, when it has a known address.

dnsHost.description: Where this domain’s DNS is hosted, from its zone’s NS records, alongside publicDns: null when the provider is not one Nightmail recognizes.

code.description: no_dns: no nameservers serve this domain: it is unregistered, lapsed or mistyped, so its records can’t be published and it can’t verify.

dnsIssue.description: Set when adding the domain (one bounded NS lookup), by Check now and by the background check: the domain has no DNS at all. Never set when DNS couldn’t be read. Fix the name (add the right domain and delete this one) or register the domain.

releasesAt.description: Hosted only: when this domain is released if its records are still unproven (72 hours after it was added). Null once ownership has been proven.

code.description: cname: the host is a CNAME, so it cannot have an MX (RFC 1034). foreign_mx: another provider receives its mail. split: other MX records share its mail. wildcard: a *.domain CNAME or MX answers for it. bane_record: it is one of Nightmail’s own names (custom MAIL FROM, ownership TXT, DKIM). host_taken: another claim, possibly in another workspace, receives on it. claimed: another workspace claimed it, or a name between it and this domain, in any scope. delegated: it is a delegated zone with its own NS records. claimed and delegated hosts never receive here. mx_missing: its MX disappeared after setup. wrong_region and null_mx: its MX points elsewhere in SES or refuses mail. proof_stale / identity_stale: the ownership TXT proof or the SES verification is out of date.

blocking.description: True when receiving there cannot work until DNS or the choice changes.

target.description: The existing CNAME target.

suggestion.description: A free subdomain to use instead.

receivingIssue.description: Hosted only: receiving needs attention. Set by the DNS checks that run when a receiving host is suggested or chosen, on Check now and in the hourly recheck. Null when the receiving record is clear.

builtIn.description: Hosted only: the workspace’s built-in domain, a subdomain of Nightmail’s own domain that needs no DNS. It sends until a domain of the workspace’s own verifies (limits here and connection.builtinDomain in GET /v1/me say what it sends), receives at every address, and can’t be deleted or changed (409 BUILTIN_DOMAIN).

scope.description: Who it sends to: anyone, or the verified addresses of the workspace’s members.

unsupported.description: Request fields a send from it can’t use (refused together, as error.details[].unsupported of 422 BUILTIN_DOMAIN_UNSUPPORTED): from (a subdomain of it), replyTo (elsewhere), headers, attachments, template, scheduledAt, kind (marketing) and campaign.

limits.description: Built-in domain only: what it sends, before a send finds out. GET /v1/domains/{id} and listDomains.

region.description: Regional BYO defaults to the first enabled region, otherwise Ohio.

url.description: Write-only HTTPS endpoint. Only the last four characters are shown; omit url on update to keep the saved URL.

headers.description: Configured names only for readers. Managers also see a masked hint and the time the header list was last replaced.

secret.description: The signing secret, whsec_ followed by 32 base64 bytes. Read it again with revealWebhookSecret.

nextStep.description: Only for a webhook tied to an MCP approval: what it depends on and how to make a lasting one.

headers.description: Write-only custom HTTP request headers, e.g. Authorization. Up to 10 unique names (case-insensitive) and 8192 UTF-8 bytes of names and values. Omit on update to keep, supply the complete list to replace, or [] to clear. Transport, Cookie and Nightmail delivery headers are reserved.

Write-only custom HTTP request headers, e.g. Authorization. Up to 10 unique names (case-insensitive) and 8192 UTF-8 bytes of names and values. Omit on update to keep, supply the complete list to replace, or [] to clear. Transport, Cookie and Nightmail delivery headers are reserved.

suppressionReason.description: Reason recorded when this send was suppressed. For a multi-recipient send blocked locally, this is the first blocked recipient in To, Cc, Bcc order.

diagnosticCode.description: A bounce or a delay: the receiving server’s reply as SES reported it, such as "smtp; 550 5.1.1 user unknown". Written by the receiving server: untrusted text, to read as data, that can hold the recipient’s address, host names and IP addresses. On the email’s own events (getEmailDetail, listEmailEvents) it is up to 500 characters, as one line without control or invisible characters. In a webhook payload and the webhook delivery log, the addresses and IP addresses in it are replaced by pattern (<address>, <ip>) and it is up to 160 characters. For several recipients, the first that has one. Absent when SES reported none, for a bounce SES generated itself (its suppression list, its address validation), and on events stored before this field.

delayType.description: A delay: SES’s reason, such as MailboxFull, SpamDetected, RecipientServerError, TransientCommunicationFailure, IPFailure or General.

expirationTime.description: A delay: when SES stops retrying the delivery (UTC).

data.description: What the event recorded. An email the content screen refused says so in code (CONTENT_REJECTED_SPAM) and nothing more: the screen’s score, its model and its threshold are never part of an event or a webhook payload.

state.description: warmup during the evaluation: until 500 real recipients were accepted and their delivery results are in (90% of them, or an hour after the 500th) (Hosted), or the first 500 emails (self-hosted).

firstEmails.description: Real recipients accepted, counted up to 500.

needed.description: Accepted recipients before the first score (500).

calibratedAt.description: When the 500th recipient was counted; the score starts once their delivery results are in, at most an hour later plus the ten-minute job run (gradedBy).

gradedBy.description: Hosted, during the evaluation once the 500th recipient was counted: the latest the first grade comes (an hour after it, plus the ten-minute job run), sooner once 90% of them have a delivery result. Null otherwise.

score.description: 0–100, one decimal; null while warming up. The quality of the last 30 days of mail, recounted hourly: 75 and up has no daily limit.

target.description: The score the evidence supports now; the score follows it on every run (the same as raw).

next.description: The next grade up and the score it starts at.

history.description: The published daily score, oldest first, up to 14 days.

key.description: complaints, content (the spam screen), bounces (to known recipients), hygiene (list quality: campaign first sends and their suppression hits; neutral without campaign mail), auth, engagement.

weight.description: Share of the score, out of 100, when every factor is measured.

value.description: The measured rate or ratio, decayed with a 30-day half-life; null when neutral.

score.description: 0–100 for this factor; null when neutral.

source.description: Neutral factors are left out and the measured ones re-weighted.

daily.description: Recipients per rolling 24 hours that admission enforces now. Null when there is no daily limit (unlimited): a workspace in good standing (score 75 and up, no warning) or an exempt one.

unlimited.description: True when no daily limit applies (daily is null): only the per-minute pace bounds sending.

source.description: calibrating: the evaluation (the first 500 real recipients); score: set by the score and the ladder, none in good standing; override: set by Nightmail; exempt: none.

band.description: The daily limit the score earns, before a resume or strike reduction. Without one: what the per-minute pace allows in 24 hours (perMinute × 1,440).

limit.description: The next band's daily limit; when unlimited, what the pace allows in 24 hours.

unlimited.description: The next band has no daily limit.

next.description: The next band up and the score it starts at. Null without a daily limit, or when an operator set it.

restore.description: After a resume: the limit is at most this many recipients a day until then (half the limit before the resume, unless an operator restored all of it).

hourly.description: Recipients the sponsor's growing workspaces may send in a rolling hour now.

used.description: Recipients sent in the rolling hour.

until.description: When the growth pace ends, after 24 clean hours.

growth.description: For 24 clean hours after the evaluation, while it limits more than the per-minute pace: sending grows from 1,000 recipients an hour (shared by the account's workspaces, every stream) to twice the distinct recipients of the last completed hour whose results are in and clean. Null otherwise. Mail over it waits in the queue.

perMinute.description: Recipients a minute the workspace may send (pacing that protects the shared pool, not a daily limit): clamp(daily ÷ 20, 50, 500), or without a daily limit a quarter of the pool's SES rate, at least 500. Half of it per sending domain.

marketingPerHour.description: Marketing recipients an hour: max(25, daily ÷ 4); without a daily limit, what the per-minute pace allows (perMinute × 60).

transactionalReserve.description: Recipients of the daily limit marketing may not use, kept for transactional mail: max(100, 10%). 0 without a daily limit and during the evaluation, whose recipients may all be marketing.

SenderLimit.description: Hosted only: the daily limit the score sets (none in good standing), the pace and what changes them.

step.description: ok; notice (dashboard only); warn (limit frozen: no rises, and a workspace without one is limited to what SES accepted from it in the last 24 hours, at least 10,000; owners emailed); restrict (marketing held, transactional flows, limit frozen); pause (all sending stopped).

pauseKind.description: bounce: only transactional bounces paused it, and an owner may resume it once in 30 days. full: complaints, the spam screen, abuse or an AWS tenant pause; an operator reviews it.

marketingRelease.description: An owner released a restrict: marketing is at this share of its allowance until then.

strikes.description: Pauses in the last 90 days. A second caps the limit at 50% for 7 days after the resume; a third needs an operator for any resume.

selfService.description: Whether an owner or admin can release this step from the dashboard (POST /v1/sender-score/release), and if not, why.

version.description: Changes with every change of standing; account.standing.changed carries it.

probation.description: Why Nightmail still checks this workspace as a new sender; null in good standing, which it reaches by itself. evaluation: its first 500 real recipients; growth: the growth pace after them; standing: a daily limit set by the score, a freeze or a strike, or a step from warn up. Until then a campaign over 500 recipients sends a list probe first, and mail is delivered as the copy the content screen read (style sheets inlined, @media and dark-mode rules left out) with the attachment allowlist, except from domains Nightmail placed on its trusted tier. The image-to-text rule applies in good standing too.

SenderStanding.description: Hosted only: the enforcement step and why.

threshold.description: The rate the line starts at.

minimum.description: The count the line also needs.

bouncedRemoved.description: Contacts that bounced or complained are removed.

listSourceConfirmed.description: Every contact opted in; no bought or old lists.

enabled.description: Usage is taken from the prepaid balance (enforcement is enforce).

enforcement.description: off or shadow: nothing is charged yet (shadow records what would be); enforce: usage is charged hourly. The balance is GET /v1/billing.

perThousand.description: Price per 1,000 emails: each recipient of a sent email, each received message. SES mailbox simulator sends count like any other send.

freeEmails.description: The sent allowance (same as freeSentEmails), kept for older clients. Sent and received each have their own allowance (freeSentEmails, freeReceivedEmails), counted separately: sends beyond theirs are charged even while received mail is still free, and the other way round.

freeSentEmails.description: Sent emails (each recipient) included free each calendar month (UTC).

freeReceivedEmails.description: Received messages included free each calendar month (UTC), separate from the sent allowance.

freeStorageBytes.description: Bytes of received mail older than 90 days stored free.

from.description: Start of the current calendar month, UTC.

sent.description: Emails created this month, each counted once however many recipients it has.

received.description: Messages received this month on any address, routed, unrouted or spam. Null unless the credential may read every received message (owners, admins and manage credentials): members and read-only keys never learn about mail they can't open.

billedSent.description: Sent emails billing counts this month, each recipient once (Hosted sending; mail canceled or rejected before it went out is taken off). The free sent allowance and the price apply to this count.

billedReceived.description: Received messages billing counts this month: mail Amazon's spam scan flagged and simulated mail are free. The free received allowance and the price apply to this count. Null like received.

cap.description: Recipients allowed per rolling 24 hours; null when this workspace has no daily limit.

used.description: Recipients charged in the rolling 24 hours, SES mailbox simulator addresses included.

resetAt.description: When capacity next frees up or the limit changes.

step.description: Index into steps of the step this workspace is on; null past them: no daily limit (cap null), or one set by the score, a warning or an operator.

daily.description: Null until the workspace connects hosted sending.

cap.description: Recipients per rolling 24 hours at this step.

requires.description: What a workspace needs to reach this step, in plain words.

steps.description: The daily limits a new workspace passes through: only the evaluation. After it, a workspace in good standing (score 75 and up, no warning) has no daily limit; bad signals set one (GET /v1/sender-score). Only real SES acceptances count: simulated sends and simulator addresses use the limit but never end the evaluation.

simulated.description: This installation simulates SES: no email leaves it, and simulated sends never count against the daily limit.

reputation.description: Account-level SES reputation from CloudWatch AWS/SES Reputation.BounceRate and Reputation.ComplaintRate, as fractions (0.05 = 5%). Latest hourly value plus 14 days of 6-hour averages. Null in reports cached before this field existed. Requires cloudwatch:GetMetricData; unavailable does not block readiness.

The most specific route wins: exact address, then the pattern with the most literal characters, then the plus-address base, then the catch-all, then the domain default.

to.description: Inbox, webhook and forward IDs, [] to keep, or 'drop'.

version.description: Ignored on apply; send the version in If-Match.

diffCount.description: Present when diff was shortened: total changed routes in this version.

diffTruncated.description: Present and true when diff was shortened to fit the response size budget; read full changes from getRoutingAudit.

via.description: The rule that sends mail here. A rule may do so for only some mail; null when routing always does.

status.description: Endpoint status; paused for a paused inbound webhook; null for inboxes and outcomes.

target.description: Where it delivers; URLs are write-only (last four characters).

call.description: How a rule calls an endpoint; null for an inbound webhook.

eventTypes.description: Events a webhook subscribes to; empty for a route-only webhook and for Slack, Discord and forward endpoints.

id.description: Nightmail domain ID.

name.description: Receiving host: the domain, or the subdomain it receives at.

hosts.description: Every host the domain receives at, or is being set up to (name is its first); addresses can be created at each.

from.description: Defaults to the public address if configured, otherwise the primary receiving address. Address keys may use only addresses owned by this mailbox.
