destination.description: A webhook ID: redeliver to that webhook only.

verificationToken.description: inbound format: the new X-Webhook-Verification-Token, which changes with the secret.

emailed.description: Whether the invitation was emailed to the invitee, with acceptUrl. When false, share acceptUrl yourself; notEmailedReason says why.

notEmailedReason.description: Why no email went out, null when one did. not_available: this installation sends no invitation email, or your account has no verified address to be named by. new_workspace: invitations are emailed once the workspace has a verified domain or has finished its evaluation. allowance_used: the invitation emails for today, or to this address, are used.

nextStep.description: What to do next, for people and agents: whether the invitee was emailed, or acceptUrl is yours to share.

workspaceName.description: The workspace’s name as plain words, at most 40 characters; empty when nothing of it can be shown.

inviterName.description: The inviter’s display name as plain words, like workspaceName; may be empty. Identify the inviter by inviterEmail.

state.description: awaiting_role: waiting for the BYO stack. provisioning: verifying regional resources and importing verified domains. ready: sending allowed once the tenant is ready. failed: the last setup attempt failed; verify again.

tenant.description: Hosted only: the SES tenant that isolates this workspace. Sends are rejected with TENANT_NOT_READY until it is ready. BYO connections are always ready.

importedDomains.description: Number of currently claimed domains imported from this BYO account.

version.description: The role template version the stack reports.

updateAvailable.description: updateConnectionStack can prepare an update to the newest template.

deleted.description: The stack was deleted in AWS.

error.description: Why the last stack was refused, to show in setup.

stack.description: A connected AWS account's CloudFormation stack (regional bring-your-own AWS only).

health.description: The connected account's last health check: what needs attention.

review.description: AWS's review of a production access request.

createdByNightmail.description: Nightmail created the identity; otherwise it was already in the account.

records.description: DNS records of an identity Nightmail created, to remove with it.

retained.description: SES identities that stay in the AWS account. Delete one in the SES console, and its DNS records, once nothing sends from it.

leftBehind.description: Resources Nightmail created but couldn't remove: its role was gone, or they were changed in AWS.

stack.description: The Nightmail stack, to delete in the CloudFormation console once the cleanup finishes.

useCase.description: How the account sends mail and to whom, for AWS's review.
useCase.example: We send receipts and account notices to our own customers, who signed up for them.

generatedAt.description: The end of the last whole UTC hour the figures cover. They change at most once an hour; responses are cached for up to 60 seconds.

available.description: False until at least 10 workspaces have sent mail in the last 30 days. Every figure is then null and regions is empty, so the figures never describe a single customer.

acceptedLast30Days.description: Emails Amazon SES accepted in the last 30 whole days of hours, rounded to two significant figures (to the nearest 10 below 100). Simulated, suppressed and rejected mail is excluded. Email history is kept for 30 days, so there is no all-time total.

acceptedLastHour.description: Emails Amazon SES accepted in the last whole UTC hour, rounded the same way. The last entry of acceptedHourly.

acceptedHourly.description: Accepted emails per whole UTC hour over the last 24 hours, oldest first, rounded. Null for an hour in which fewer than 3 workspaces sent.

deliveryRate.description: delivered ÷ (delivered + bounced) for emails created in the last 30 days, each email counted once, to three decimals. Null without outcomes.

medianSendLatencyMs.description: Median time from API acceptance to Amazon SES acceptance for the most recent 5,000 direct, unscheduled sends in the last 24 whole hours, to the nearest 10 ms. Null without samples from at least 3 workspaces.

regions.description: AWS regions that accepted mail in the last 30 days. Hosted installations list only their shared sending regions.

allOf.description: The ten newest domains, exactly as listDomains with limit=10 and refresh=false returns them (continue there with nextCursor). Null when listDomains would refuse the caller, such as a member or a self-hosted installation without live SES.

apiKeys.description: Null when listApiKeys would refuse the caller: it needs unrestricted manage, and agent tokens never list keys.

any.description: Whether any email the caller can read exists. Same scope as listEmails: a domain-restricted key sees only direct sends from its domains.

webhooks.description: Null when listWebhooks would refuse the caller: members and domain-restricted keys.

invitations.description: Null unless listWorkspaceInvitations would answer: an owner or admin dashboard session on a hosted installation.

campaign.description: A campaign exists, draft or not.

campaignSent.description: A campaign was launched (preparing, scheduled, sending, paused or done).

readers.description: A newsletter has a reader (a member of its list).

issueSent.description: A campaign to a newsletter was launched.

agent.description: An agent is connected: an unrevoked API key an agent setup made (the agent prompt's setup token or a device code), or a member's active MCP sign-in that defaults to this workspace or made agent tokens here.

progress.description: The first steps of each focus (focus in getWorkspaceSettings) and whether an agent is connected, as yes or no. Null unless the caller manages the whole workspace.

id.description: The support reference (sho_…). Quote it to support.

url.description: Where to continue with support, carrying the signed handoff; null when no support site is configured.

token.description: The signed handoff (EdDSA JWS, 10 minutes), or null when signing is not configured.

expiresAt.description: Until when support can use this handoff to open read access (30 minutes, once).

enforcement.description: off: nothing is metered for billing. shadow: usage is recorded and priced but nothing is charged. enforce: usage is taken from the balance hourly.

mode.description: prepaid: usage is taken from the balance. exempt: the workspace is free (see freePlan).

sending.description: paused: sends get 402 BALANCE_EXHAUSTED until credit is added.

receiving.description: grace: the balance is below $0 and received mail is still accepted until grace.receiveHoldAt; held: new received mail is stored but not delivered until a top-up. While the installation doesn’t hold received mail, receiving stays ok.

allOf.description: Promotional credit: spent first, never refunded.
Usage not yet taken from the balance (settled hourly).

balance.description: Null unless the caller is an owner or admin session, or a manage key or grant.

used.description: Used this month, settled and unsettled.

emails.description: The sent allowance (same as sent), kept for older clients. Each direction has its own allowance: see sent and received.

used.description: Used this month, settled and unsettled.

sent.description: Free sent emails this month, each recipient counting once. Sends beyond it are charged even while received mail is still free.

used.description: Used this month, settled and unsettled.

received.description: Free received messages this month, separate from the sent allowance. Null unless the credential may read every received message (owners, admins and manage credentials), as in GET /v1/usage.

agedBytes.description: Bytes of received mail older than 90 days.

allOf.description: This month’s usage cost after the free allowance, settled and unsettled, charged or not.

receiveHoldAt.description: When new received mail starts being held; null when nothing is owed or the installation doesn’t hold received mail.

disabledReason.description: Why Nightmail turned auto-recharge off (a card decline code, dispute or a removed card).

emailPerThousand.description: USD per 1,000 emails, sent (per recipient) or received (per message).

decisionPerThousand.description: Deprecated: AI decisions are free, so this is always "0.00".

storagePerGbMonth.description: USD per GB-month for received mail older than 90 days, beyond the free GB.

freeEmails.description: The sent allowance (same as freeSentEmails), kept for older clients. Each direction has its own allowance, counted separately (freeSentEmails, freeReceivedEmails).

freeSentEmails.description: Sent emails (each recipient) free each calendar month (UTC).

freeReceivedEmails.description: Received messages free each calendar month (UTC), separate from the sent allowance.

until.description: When the free plan ends; null: no end date.

freePlan.description: Set when Anomaly made this workspace free (mode exempt): nothing is charged and sending never pauses for the balance. Usage is still measured, and monthToDate shows what it would cost.

quantity.description: send: recipients; receive: messages; omen: emails checked by AI decisions, which are free (the meter keeps its name from before the rename); storage: billable byte-days beyond the free GB; byo_*: reported only, $0.

allOf.description: paid + promo; negative takes from the balance.
Paid and promotional balance after this entry.

expiresAt.description: For a top-up: when its remaining credit expires, 12 months after purchase. Unused credit is not refundable.

thresholdCents.description: Recharge when the balance falls below this ($5 to $1,000).

amountCents.description: Credit to add each time ($20 to $10,000).

monthlyCapCents.description: At most this much auto-recharge per calendar month (UTC), at least amountCents and up to $250,000.

ticketId.description: The support ticket it was filed as.

redacted.description: How many values that looked like keys, tokens or passwords were removed from message and context.

message.description: What happened and what would have made it easier. Plain text. Anything that looks like a key, token or password is removed before it is stored.

requestId.description: The request ID of a call that went wrong: its x-request-id header, or error.requestId.

operation.description: The operation or MCP tool involved, such as sendEmail.

context.description: What you were trying to do, in a sentence or two.

patch.description: Changes anything about a key and keeps its secret, so nothing has to be redeployed: name and expiresAt on any key; a workspace key's permissions and sender domains (replace them with domains, or addDomains and removeDomains); a key for addresses or an inbox's access: its addresses (addressIds, addAddressIds, removeAddressIds), its mail (create included), its inbox (inboxId), or access.type to make an inbox key a key for addresses or back. A workspace key stays a workspace key. Takes effect from the next request: requests already waiting lose what was removed, and mail the key queued is sent only within its new access. Each change is recorded with who made it, before and after (lastChange, listApiKeyChanges, Activity). Needs the access createApiKey needs, checked again as the change is written, and no key changes itself. An agent signed in over MCP as a person changes any key that person could change in the dashboard; a key an MCP approval created changes only keys that approval created; temporary agent tokens change none. Revoked keys and keys whose inbox ended can't be changed; an expired key can be given a later expiry.

Reusing a key with a different body returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Keys are scoped to the API key and request path. post.summary: Poll for the agent's API key
post.description: With the device code from startAgentDeviceAuthorization, every interval seconds until the person decides. Each answer follows RFC 8628: 400 AUTHORIZATION_PENDING (keep polling), 400 SLOW_DOWN (polled too soon: wait five seconds longer from now on), 400 ACCESS_DENIED (the person denied it: stop), 400 EXPIRED_TOKEN (start again), or 201 with the API key, once. A poll after that gets 409 DEVICE_CODE_USED naming the key it gave (error.details: keyId, name, prefix, issuedAt, revokedAt), never the key again and never a second one: use the key you saved. Retry-After gives the seconds to wait.

post.summary: Check email sendability without sending
post.description: Read-only 0–100 advisory score, not an inbox-placement probability or admission decision. Supply one draft (HTML or text), outbound email ID, or campaign ID. Uses visible retained content, cached From-domain facts, and workspace reputation for unrestricted readers. No DNS/asset fetches or paid screen. Marketing drafts are checked as supplied; Nightmail adds the unsubscribe headers, the link and the workspace’s postal address to campaigns and to marketing mail it sent, so those are checked as sent. Each finding’s fix is one plain sentence and fixIn says where it is made. MIME bytes are estimated.

post.description: Front-door admission and content screening: Hosted sending checks validation, recipient suppression/consent, balance, limits, and the outbound harm screen synchronously before queueing. Failing messages return an immediate error (422 RECIPIENT_INELIGIBLE, 422 CONTENT_REJECTED_SPAM, 422 CONTENT_TOO_LARGE_TO_SCREEN, or retryable 503 CONTENT_SCREEN_UNAVAILABLE with Retry-After when no mandatory classifier is configured) and nothing is queued; during a temporary outage of both classifiers, eligible mail is accepted (202) and held unscreened until a classifier answers. Screened-text limits: at most 65,536 UTF-8 bytes per message (installation default) and 150 distinct link hosts (3,000 bytes of host names), counting link labels that name another host; over either limit, error.details[0] holds { screenedBytes, limitBytes } or { linkHosts, linkHostLimit } (plus index in a batch). Marketing ramp: on Hosted sending, a workspace still ramping up (a new sender, exempt and first-party ones included) sends kind: marketing at most its ramp step's hourly ceiling (1,000, 2,500, 5,000, 10,000, 20,000, 40,000, 75,000, 150,000, 300,000 recipients an hour), shared with its campaigns. A send that would cross it is refused with nothing queued (a batch as a whole): retryable 429 RAMP_LIMIT_REACHED, with Retry-After (seconds until more room opens) and error.details[0] holding { step, steps, ceilingPerHour, usedThisHour, fitsNow, requested, stepOpensAt }. A scheduled marketing send is refused the same way when it is scheduled if it is larger than the step's whole ceiling, or if with the marketing already scheduled within 24 hours either side of its time it is more than the step sends in 24 hours (error.details[0] adds { scheduledBacklog, dailyBudget }); one that fits is held at its time until its hour has room (it stays scheduled, scheduledAt moving to when it tries again, with a dispatch_deferred event), never rejected for the ramp. While the workspace ramps and a campaign of it is stopped by the automatic pause, the list probe or the ramp's check (LIST_QUALITY, BOUNCE_RATE_HIGH, COMPLAINT_RATE_HIGH) and not resumed or canceled, marketing sends and schedules are refused with 409 RAMP_PAUSED (not retryable; error.details[0] holds { campaignId, pauseCode }): review and resume that campaign first. For a large list, send a campaign instead: campaigns are paced automatically. Transactional mail is never ramped or paused by it. Built-in domain (Hosted): every workspace has a subdomain of Nightmail's own domain (connection.builtinDomain in GET /v1/me) that sends until the workspace verifies a domain of its own: plain transactional email sent now, without attachments, custom headers, a stored template or a Reply-To elsewhere (422 BUILTIN_DOMAIN_UNSUPPORTED, once, listing every such field in error.details[].unsupported), to the recipients the installation allows (on hosted Nightmail, for now, only the verified sign-in addresses of the workspace's members: 422 BUILTIN_DOMAIN_RECIPIENT names any other recipient in error.details[0].notMembers; add a domain of your own to email anyone), within a per-minute and a daily recipient cap (429 BUILTIN_DOMAIN_LIMIT), screened like a new sender's mail. Once a domain of its own verifies it stops sending and answers 409 OWN_DOMAIN_VERIFIED, with the same address at that domain to use instead in error.details[0].suggestedFrom (and every verified domain in verifiedDomains). Attachments: One file is at most 8 MiB decoded when sent as base64 in JSON (POST /v1/attachments), or 25 MiB as raw bytes (POST /v1/attachments/upload, with the name URI-encoded in X-Nightmail-Filename and the type in Content-Type). One email carries at most 100 files and 25 MiB of them together, decoded. A workspace keeps at most 100 GiB of uploaded files. For anything larger, link to the file from the email. filename: the file's name: 1 to 200 characters, without control characters, / or \, and not an extension Amazon SES refuses (.exe, .bat, .js, .vbs and others). contentType: a MIME type such as application/pdf (type/subtype, optionally with ; parameters), at most 78 printable ASCII characters. disposition: attachment (the default) or inline; inline needs a contentId: 1 to 78 letters, digits, _ . @ or -, for an inline image the HTML shows as cid:<contentId>, unique within the email. Upload each file once, then list its ID in the email's attachments. A send with attachment problems is refused once, naming every problem: error.details lists each with its email (index, in a batch), attachment (its position in attachments), id, filename, code and message. Hosted senders on probation attach only standard types (images, PDF, office documents, archives, audio, video, plain text) whose name, declared type and content agree, inline only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP images, and never SVG.

schema.description: Optional. Makes retries safe. Repeating a request with the same key and the same body returns the original result without performing the write again. While the first request with a key is still running, a duplicate returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with Retry-After: retry with the same key, never a new one. Reusing a key with a different body returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Keys are scoped to the API key and request path. A send's key is kept at least 30 days from the request, as long as the log of the emails it queued; then it is deleted, and the same key is a new request that sends again. A scheduled send's key is kept at least 60 days, after which a repeat is refused because its time has passed. Without a key, every request is processed, so a retried send can deliver twice.

post.description: Uploads one file as base64 in JSON; list the returned id in an email's attachments. For files over 8 MiB, POST /v1/attachments/upload takes the raw bytes as the body, with the fields in headers: X-Nightmail-Filename (URI-encoded), Content-Type, X-Nightmail-Disposition and X-Nightmail-Content-Id; 422 ATTACHMENT_METADATA_INVALID names every header that is wrong, what it held and what it must be. Attachments: One file is at most 8 MiB decoded when sent as base64 in JSON (POST /v1/attachments), or 25 MiB as raw bytes (POST /v1/attachments/upload, with the name URI-encoded in X-Nightmail-Filename and the type in Content-Type). One email carries at most 100 files and 25 MiB of them together, decoded. A workspace keeps at most 100 GiB of uploaded files. For anything larger, link to the file from the email. filename: the file's name: 1 to 200 characters, without control characters, / or \, and not an extension Amazon SES refuses (.exe, .bat, .js, .vbs and others). contentType: a MIME type such as application/pdf (type/subtype, optionally with ; parameters), at most 78 printable ASCII characters. disposition: attachment (the default) or inline; inline needs a contentId: 1 to 78 letters, digits, _ . @ or -, for an inline image the HTML shows as cid:<contentId>, unique within the email. Upload each file once, then list its ID in the email's attachments. A send with attachment problems is refused once, naming every problem: error.details lists each with its email (index, in a batch), attachment (its position in attachments), id, filename, code and message. Hosted senders on probation attach only standard types (images, PDF, office documents, archives, audio, video, plain text) whose name, declared type and content agree, inline only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or BMP images, and never SVG.

get.description: Lifetime campaign delivery and unique open/click statistics, progress, tracking setting and rates with numeric numerators/denominators. Counts distinct emails across all stored feedback, not event occurrences. Delivery/bounce/complaint rates use accepted emails; open/click rates use delivered emails. Both rate counts exclude simulated emails. Rates are fractions, null for zero denominators; engagement rates are also null with tracking disabled. Delivered means receiving-server acceptance, not inbox placement. Engagement includes bots/privacy proxies. Done means dispatch finished; asynchronous feedback can still change totals. A campaign of at least 20,000 recipients is counted in the background: about once a minute while it sends (every few minutes for the largest, so counting stays a small share of the database's time), once more when it finishes, and again when read more than 10 minutes later if anything changed. Its figures are the last count, so they can be minutes old; computedAt says when. A finished campaign keeps its figures after its emails leave the 30-day history. Each statement stops after 5 seconds: a request that needs longer is refused with 422 READ_TOO_LARGE. Narrow the dates or filters.

post.description: Send the current draft, personalized with data, to one address as a transactional test. On Hosted sending a test goes only to an address the workspace has proven is its own: a member’s verified email, an address at one of its currently verified domains or their subdomains (its receiving addresses and inboxes there included; not a domain whose verification lapsed), or the SES mailbox simulator (422 TEST_RECIPIENT_NOT_OWNED otherwise; send the campaign to reach anyone else), a workspace sends at most 20 tests a clock hour (429 CAMPAIGN_TEST_LIMIT, retryable at resetAt), and each test is screened on its own, with the campaign limit (131,072 bytes of screened text by default; 422 CONTENT_TOO_LARGE_TO_SCREEN with error.details[0] { screenedBytes, limitBytes } over it).

post.description: Accept the current revision for durable background delivery: small audiences (<=5,000 list members) freeze immediately while larger audiences freeze in the background during preparing, every message is validated before sending, then recipients are released into the dispatch queue. The 202 queued count is recipients expected (not SES acceptance or delivery); delivery.total on GET /v1/campaigns/{id} is authoritative once the audience is frozen. Every email’s footer shows the workspace’s postal address under the Unsubscribe link, as US law (CAN-SPAM) requires, frozen as it is now: without one the request is refused with 422 POSTAL_ADDRESS_REQUIRED (set postalAddress with updateWorkspaceSettings). Hosted campaigns screen every distinct copy during launch and prepare before any row enters the sending queue, each distinct copy only once: recipients whose personalized copies read the same share one verdict. The campaign’s own copy, placeholders unresolved, is screened first and may hold 131,072 bytes of screened text (installation default; 422 CONTENT_TOO_LARGE_TO_SCREEN with error.details[0] { screenedBytes, limitBytes } otherwise); so may each copy. A failing copy never enters the sending queue (CONTENT_REJECTED_SPAM); when refused copies pass 5% and 10 recipients the campaign pauses once for review, and a positive verdict on the campaign’s own copy fails it before anyone is sent to. Audiences on lists up to 5,000 members freeze inside this request; larger audiences freeze in the background during preparing so this request returns immediately. CampaignQueued.queued is recipients expected; delivery.total on GET /v1/campaigns/{id} is authoritative once the audience is frozen. Late capture failures (such as EMPTY_AUDIENCE or AUDIENCE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) move the campaign to failed with delivery.error and leave the draft editable.

post.description: Hosted only. Choose a host for this domain to receive on, its root or one of its subdomains. Until the domain receives anywhere, the choice replaces the automatic suggestion (the first of reply., inbound., mail. and so on with no MX and no CNAME), and null returns to it. Once it receives, the chosen host is added beside the hosts it already receives on, as POST /v1/inbound/domains/{id}/hosts does: nothing that receives is moved or stopped. Public DNS is checked first. A CNAME (RFC 1034), one of Nightmail’s own names (custom MAIL FROM, ownership TXT, DKIM), a host another domain receives on (in any workspace), a name another workspace has claimed (send-only included) or a delegated zone (its own NS records) is refused with a free subdomain to use instead. A host whose mail another provider receives, or whose MX is split, needs confirm: true, because publishing Nightmail’s MX moves that mail. A wildcard (*.domain) answer only flags receivingIssue. Nothing changes in DNS or SES.

Selects emails created in [from,to), scoped by email region and stream. to defaults to now and from to 24 hours (granularity=10m) or 30 days before to; from equal to to is an empty window. Each outcome counts distinct emails, so replays do not inflate counts and outcomes may overlap. Accepted (bucket sent) means evidence of provider acceptance, not merely queued/created. Daily UTC creation buckets contain count=created emails. Granularity defaults to day; granularity=hour returns hourly UTC creation buckets and granularity=10m returns 10-minute UTC creation buckets (within the last 6 days) with canonical ISO dates, while preserving daily buckets and totals. Absent buckets mean zero created emails and zero outcomes; no moving averages are applied. Engagement is observed, not verified human activity. get.description: The workspace sender score, the daily limit it sets and the enforcement step (Hosted). In good standing (a score of 75 or more, no warning) there is no daily limit: limit.unlimited is true, limit.daily null, and only the per-minute pace (limit.perMinute) applies. A new workspace's first 500 real recipients are its evaluation, at 500 a day until their delivery results are in (gradedBy says by when); for 24 clean hours after it, sending grows from 1,000 recipients an hour, doubling with each clean hour (limit.growth). Under 75 the limit is 500 (70–74), 200 (65–69) or 100, and a warning freezes it. The score (0–100) is the quality of what the workspace sends (complaints, the spam screen, bounces, list quality, authentication and engagement), decayed with a 30-day half-life and recounted hourly. Self-hosted and BYO get the score for display only. post.summary: Create an agent inbox
post.description: Creates an inbox with a fresh address. Set type=persistent for forever retention (no lease or default per-inbox cap; workspace manage permission). The default is an expiring inbox on one of the workspace’s active receiving domains, or a sandbox inbox that needs no DNS. Then wait for mail with GET /v1/inboxes/{id}/messages?wait=30 (or the SDK’s waitForMessage). Needs a workspace admin or a key with create permission. Limits: 60 creates per minute and 50,000 retained inboxes (including grace and pending erasure) per workspace. Errors: RECEIVING_DOMAIN_REQUIRED and RECEIVING_NOT_ACTIVE name the DNS step to take; ADDRESS_TAKEN, ADDRESS_RETIRED, EPHEMERAL_INBOX_LIMIT, INBOX_CREATE_RATE (with Retry-After) and IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

type.description: persistent: a real address kept until explicitly deleted. ephemeral: a real address on one of your active receiving domains. sandbox: an address on a .invalid host that receives nothing from the internet; fill it with POST /v1/inboxes/{id}/simulate.

ttlSeconds.description: Lifetime before the inbox expires: 60 seconds to 30 days. Default 24 hours.

graceHours.description: Hours after expiry during which new mail is still stored but held, before everything is erased. 0–168, default 24.

domain.description: Receiving host for the address, such as reply.acme.com. Default: the workspace’s oldest active receiving host.

localPart.description: Admin REST only; provisioning keys and MCP must omit this. Default: 10 random characters, which nobody can guess.

name.description: A label for the dashboard and lists. Replies use it as the From display name.

metadata.description: Your own JSON, up to 16 KiB. Returned as is.

clientId.description: Idempotency key. Repeating a create with the same clientId and body returns the same inbox (200, without the key secret); a different body is a 409.

messages.description: Messages delivered before new mail is held. At most 200.

bytes.description: Stored bytes before new mail is held. At most 25 MiB.

limits.description: Optional delivery caps. Temporary inboxes default to 200 messages and 25 MiB; persistent inboxes have no default delivery cap. Held mail is stored and readable, never dropped.

enabled.description: Allow replies through POST /v1/inbound/threads/{threadId}/reply.

perDay.description: Deprecated and not enforced: replies have no daily cap. Accepted for compatibility.

send.description: Replies only go to people who wrote to this inbox, within the loop guards and the workspace’s sending limits. Sandbox inboxes never send.

permissions.description: read: list and read mail. modify: mark read, simulate, delete the inbox. send: reply (needs send.enabled).

credential.description: Also create a key that can use only this inbox. Its secret is returned once and it expires with the inbox. Use it as a bearer token for this API or hosted MCP.

get.summary: List or wait for inbox messages
get.description: Oldest first, in commit order. Without after, the page starts at the first message, so mail that arrived before the call is included. With wait, the call holds until a matching message arrives or the time runs out, and answers as soon as the message is stored; pass the returned cursor as after on the next call. Pages are also bounded by response size and may return fewer than limit messages while hasMore is true; to returns at most 20 addresses with the total in toCount. Junk, unverified and held mail never wake a waiter: list them with include=held. Each waited second counts as one request against the key’s per-minute budget. Filtered queries: Each statement stops after 5 seconds: a request that needs longer is refused with 422 READ_TOO_LARGE. Narrow the dates or filters.

post.summary: Tell Nightmail what got in your way
post.description:
Tell Nightmail what got in your way while doing a task: what happened and what would have made it easier, with the request ID of a call that went wrong if you have one. Only message is needed; any other field (such as severity or kind, which an earlier version asked for) is ignored. It is filed as a support ticket for the Nightmail team, who read every one, with this credential's workspace and the key, sign-in or token that sent it; no reply comes back, so carry on with the task after sending it.

Any credential that can read may send it (API keys, including ones limited to sender domains, agent tokens and MCP sign-ins), for its own workspace: at most 20 reports an hour from one credential and 50 from one workspace (429 FEEDBACK_RATE_LIMITED, with Retry-After). Anything in message or context that looks like a key, token or password is removed before it is stored; redacted says how many. Send one report per distinct problem.
